title: Local anaesthetics & allergy in skin surgery
summary: Lidocaine maximum doses (BNF: 200 mg plain, 500 mg with adrenaline), how to calculate them, adrenaline cautions, local anaesthetic systemic toxicity, topical anaesthetics and allergy to latex, chlorhexidine or local anaesthetic.

glance.think: Planning or checking a local anaesthetic dose, or a patient reporting an ‘allergy’ to local anaesthetic, latex or skin prep.
glance.engine: Sodium-channel blockade stops nerve conduction; adrenaline prolongs action and reduces bleeding; overdose affects brain and heart.
glance.backbone: 1% = 10 mg/ml; BNF maximum 200 mg plain and 500 mg with adrenaline (weight-based 3 and 7 mg/kg as a cross-check); reduce in frailty, liver disease and heart failure; latex-free room and alternative prep for allergy.
glance.never_miss: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (perioral tingling, seizures, arrhythmia): stop, call for help, AAGBI/Intralipid protocol; chlorhexidine anaphylaxis.

what: Amide local anaesthetics (lidocaine, prilocaine, bupivacaine, levobupivacaine, articaine, mepivacaine) and esters (tetracaine/amethocaine, benzocaine, chloroprocaine) block voltage-gated sodium channels in nerves. **Adrenaline** is added for vasoconstriction: less bleeding, longer action, and a higher maximum dose.

what.h: Allergy: latex, chlorhexidine and local anaesthetic

list: **Latex allergy** is either **type I** (IgE-mediated: urticaria, rhinitis, asthma, **anaphylaxis**) or **type IV** (allergic contact dermatitis to rubber accelerators: thiurams, carbamates, MBT). Irritant hand dermatitis from gloves is not an allergy.
**Chlorhexidine** is an increasingly recognised cause of **perioperative anaphylaxis** (MHRA 2012 alert). It is found in skin preps, catheters, lubricants and wipes.

cause.h: Allergy: latex, chlorhexidine and local anaesthetic

list: Healthcare workers.
**Spina bifida and multiple childhood surgeries.**
Atopy.
**Latex–fruit syndrome**: cross-reaction with **banana, avocado, kiwi, chestnut** and others.

features.h: Lidocaine maximum dose (BNF): the key Case 1 calculation

head: BNF adult maximum (infiltration)
Weight-based convention (common teaching)
rows: **Up to 3 mg/kg** (check the BNFC entry and age band)

list: **Use ideal body weight in obesity.** **Reduce the dose in frail elderly people, in hepatic impairment, in heart failure** (reduced clearance), and in highly vascular sites (absorption).

**[Case 1](condition:skin-surgery-preop), worked (teaching only):** 60 kg × 7 mg/kg = **420 mg** with adrenaline. This is below the BNF absolute ceiling of 500 mg. At 2% (20 mg/ml), 420 mg is **21 ml** (course teaching rounded to "20 ml"). **Plain** lidocaine at 3 mg/kg is 180 mg = **9 ml of 2%** (and under the 200 mg BNF cap). For a small DF excision, the volume actually used is typically a **few millilitres**, far below the maximum.

**Note on 1:80,000 adrenaline:** lidocaine 2% with adrenaline 1:80,000 is the **dental cartridge** formulation. For skin surgery in UK practice, **1% or 2% with 1:200,000 adrenaline** is more usual. The maximum-dose principle is the same.

features.h: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST): recognise and respond

list: **Early (CNS):** perioral numbness or tingling, **metallic taste**, tinnitus, light-headedness, visual disturbance, slurred speech, agitation or drowsiness.
**Late:** muscle twitching → **seizures** → coma; **cardiovascular:** bradycardia, arrhythmias, hypotension, **cardiac arrest** (bupivacaine is most cardiotoxic).

**Response (Association of Anaesthetists LAST guideline):** stop injecting; call for help (999 in community settings); airway, 100% oxygen, ABC; treat seizures (benzodiazepine); CPR if arrested; **IV 20% lipid emulsion** (Intralipid®) per the guideline, where available. Settings using larger LA volumes should know where it is kept
**Prevention:** calculate the maximum dose before starting, **aspirate before injecting**, inject slowly, use the lowest effective volume, and keep patients under observation.
**Distinguish from vasovagal** (pallor, sweating, bradycardia, quick recovery when lying flat; the commonest event) and **adrenaline effect** (palpitations, tremor, anxiety, tachycardia).

features: **True LA allergy** is rare. Most "allergies" are vasovagal, adrenaline effects or anxiety. **Ester allergy (PABA)** does not cross-react with amides. **Methylparaben** (the course point) is a preservative in **multi-dose vials** and can cause reactions in paraben-sensitive patients, so use **single-dose, preservative-free ampoules**. Refer suspected LA allergy for allergy testing before elective surgery.

features: Topicals reduce needle pain. They **do not** provide surgical anaesthesia for an excision.

features.h: Allergy: latex, chlorhexidine and local anaesthetic

features: Type I reactions within minutes of contact: urticaria, angioedema, wheeze, hypotension. Type IV: eczema at the contact site 24–72 h later.

diagnosis.h: Allergy: latex, chlorhexidine and local anaesthetic

diagnosis: History. Specific IgE to latex (k82) and components (Hev b 1, 3, 5, 6.01); skin prick test; patch testing for type IV.

differentials.h: Allergy: latex, chlorhexidine and local anaesthetic

differentials: Irritant glove dermatitis; reaction to chlorhexidine, LA (rare), antibiotics, or adhesive dressings (acrylates, colophony); vasovagal syncope.

management.h: Allergy: latex, chlorhexidine and local anaesthetic

list: **First on the list** (the course answer) so latex particles in the room are minimised. A **latex-free environment**: nitrile or neoprene gloves, latex-free tourniquets, BP cuffs, catheters, dressings and drug vial stoppers (check), and a sign on the door.
**Prepared anaphylaxis kit.**
Document the allergy clearly (type and reaction) in the record and referral.
**IM adrenaline 1 mg/ml (1:1000): adults and children >12 years 500 micrograms (0.5 ml)**, into the anterolateral thigh. **Repeat after 5 minutes** if there is no improvement.
Lie flat (or sit up if breathless), legs raised; call 999; high-flow oxygen; IV fluids if trained.
**Antihistamines and steroids are not first-line** (RCUK 2021 de-emphasised them for the emergency phase).
Refractory anaphylaxis (two IM doses without improvement) needs specialist help urgently.
**Mast cell tryptase** samples (as soon as possible, at 1–2 h and at 24 h or later) and **referral to an allergy clinic** (NICE CG134).

management: **Chlorhexidine:** for an allergic patient use an alternative prep, e.g. **povidone-iodine** if not allergic, or alcohol alone.
red_flags: Perioral tingling, metallic taste, confusion, seizures or arrhythmia after injection: **local anaesthetic systemic toxicity**, stop, 999 and lipid emulsion per the AAGBI guideline.
Never exceed the **BNF maximum**: lidocaine 200 mg plain or 500 mg with adrenaline (adult).
pearls: Warm, buffered lidocaine (with 8.4% sodium bicarbonate, 1:10) injected slowly through a fine needle reduces pain (practitioner technique; local policy).
Tell the patient the numbness lasts 1–3 h (longer with bupivacaine). Avoid hot drinks or biting the lip after facial or oral blocks.

pearls.h: Allergy: latex, chlorhexidine and local anaesthetic

pearls: **Adrenaline auto-injector** patients: check they carry **two** devices in date (MHRA 2017 advice), and that they know latex is hidden in balloons, condoms, rubber gloves and some dental and medical products.
Latex-fruit syndrome foods may cause oral allergy or anaphylaxis.
